title: Add dynamicTreemapPadding setting for adaptive outer padding reduction
description:
## Problem

The current treemap layout validator only uses weight boosting to fix collapsed or extreme-aspect-ratio nodes. In dense trees, boosting weights alone is often insufficient because parent containers lose too much space to paddingOuter, leaving their children with effectively zero or extreme geometry.

## Goal

Add a new VS Code setting 	estextension.dynamicTreemapPadding (boolean, default 	rue). When enabled, the layout validator will run its existing Phase 1 (exponential bracketing) and Phase 2 (binary search refinement) as usual, and then—if problems persist—enter a new **Phase 3** that progressively shrinks paddingOuter for container nodes whose children are collapsed or extreme. Phase 3 is **additive** to Phase 2: weights are **not restored** before or between Phase 3 attempts; padding reduction is layered on top of whatever weight state Phase 2 left behind.

## Implementation Plan

1. **Settings schema** (package.json, src/visualization/interfaces/messages.ts)
   - Add 	estextension.dynamicTreemapPadding boolean property.
   - Add dynamicTreemapPadding: boolean to ExtensionConfig.
   - Regenerate src/generated/settingsSchema.ts.

2. **Layout interface** (src/visualization/interfaces/layout.ts)
   - Add paddingOuterOverrides?: Map<string, number> to TreemapLayoutConfig.

3. **Treemap layout** (src/visualization/layout/treemapLayout.ts)
   - Update paddingOuter callback to check paddingOuterOverrides by node ID.
   - Apply the override factor to the dynamically computed padding, then clamp to the per-node pixel minimum (vgSide * MIN_PADDIN_PERC).

4. **Layout validator** (src/visualization/webview/render/treemapLayoutValidator.ts)
   - Accept dynamicTreemapPadding?: boolean in computeValidatedLayout.
   - After Phase 2 completes, if dynamicTreemapPadding is true and  estProblemCount > 0, enter Phase 3 (up to 4 attempts):
     - **Do NOT call estoreWeights** before Phase 3.
     - Use  estResult's problem parent IDs as the initial set of parents whose paddingOuter should be reduced.
     - Maintain a paddingOuterOverrides map; halve the factor for each affected parent on every attempt (initial factor = 0.5, then 0.25, etc.).
     - Re-run TreemapLayout.compute() with the override map.
     - Track the best result across Phase 3 attempts.
     - Stop early if a clean layout (0 problems) is found.
     - Update the problem parent IDs from each attempt so that newly affected parents are also targeted.
   - Only restore original weights **after** Phase 3 completes (just before returning).

5. **Render manager** (src/visualization/webview/render/treemap.ts)
   - Pass 	his.settings.dynamicTreemapPadding into computeValidatedLayout.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] package.json contains the new boolean setting with appropriate default and description.
- [ ] src/generated/settingsSchema.ts is regenerated and includes the new setting.
- [ ] ExtensionConfig carries dynamicTreemapPadding into the webview.
- [ ] TreemapLayoutConfig supports paddingOuterOverrides.
- [ ] 	reemapLayout.ts respects overrides while keeping MIN_PADDIN_PERC as a hard floor.
- [ ] 	reemapLayoutValidator.ts implements Phase 3 only when the setting is enabled, without restoring weights between Phase 2 and Phase 3 or between Phase 3 attempts.
- [ ] 	reemap.ts wires the setting through to the validator.
- [ ] pnpm run compile succeeds with both extension and webview TypeScript targets.
- [ ] pnpm run lint passes.
notes:
Validator algorithm redesigned:
- Removed Phase 2 (binary search)
- Weight-boost phase now compares each attempt with the previous; stops and switches to padding if strictly worse
- Comparison uses problemCount first, then extremeMetric (sum of aspect ratios for extreme nodes)
- Padding-reduction phase restores weights to the best weight-boost attempt, then iteratively halves paddingOuter for problem parents
- Padding stops if a padding attempt is strictly worse than the previous padding attempt
- Constants renamed: PHASE1_ATTEMPTS → MAX_WEIGHT_BOOST_ATTEMPTS, PHASE3_ATTEMPTS → MAX_PADDING_REDUCTION_ATTEMPTS

title: Restyle settings webview to match native VS Code
description:
## Goal
Make the settings webview (SettingsWebviewProvider panel + sidebar popup) look indistinguishable from native VS Code settings.

## Scope
- media/settings/settings.css — main stylesheet
- media/settings/settings.html — add codicon CSS link
- src/SettingsHtmlBuilder.ts — add section headers, descriptions, modified indicators, icons
- media/settings/settings.js — add modified indicator toggle, focus management
- src/visualization/graphTemplate.html — sync inline popup styles

## Visual Targets
- Use --vscode-settings-* CSS variables (headerForeground, rowHoverBackground, modifiedItemIndicator, etc.)
- Font-weight 600 for labels, descriptionForeground for descriptions
- Row padding 8px 10px 12px, gap 4px
- Modified indicator: 2px left border with settings-modifiedItemIndicator
- Focus ring: 1px solid settings-focusedRowBorder
- Input widths: 100% for sidebar context
- Codicon icons for reset, warnings, info
- Section headers with settings-headerForeground

value: Settings webview restyled to match native VS Code: uses --vscode-settings-* CSS variables, font-weight 600 labels, descriptionForeground for descriptions, modified indicator (is-configured class), focus-within rings, section headers, codicon icons. Descriptions now included in generated schema.
